summary: Residency stamp rotation leads to TLS session mismatch with CDN -> client-observed p50/p95 latency increase
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent increase in end-to-end latency after we rotated residency stamps for a subset of tokens during a control-plane reconciliation window. The increase appears only for requests that are routed through our CDN-prefetch path and then hand off to a different edge SNI than expected.

Impact:
- BrightHealth AI (Dedicated) reports p50 increased from ~120ms to ~420ms and p95 from ~900ms to ~2.6s for text-generation requests over a 20 minute window.
- Errors: no 5xxs reported from runtime; increased TLS renegotiation counts and handshake time recorded at edge.

Environment:
- prod, customer tenant on Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with eu-west failover.
- Residency mode: safe-residency (control-plane stamp rotation enabled).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send steady 10rps requests pinned to eu-west token that was recently rotated.
2) Observe client-side timing and server-provided X-Residency-Stamp header.
3) Occasionally requests route via CDN edge A (us-east) which has different TLS session cache for the customer, causing full handshake.

Observed behavior:
- TLS full-handshake durations spike for affected requests (200-800ms).
- Edge reports SNI flip between requests associated with same token within a short TTL window.
- Control-plane logs show residency-stamp update at 14:12:03 UTC, followed by route reconcilers pushing mapping at 14:12:09 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Residency stamp rotation should not produce mixed-egress where same token alternates SNI/edge within session lifespan and cause new TLS handshakes.

Logs / artifacts:
- Edge TLS metrics link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/edge/tls-handshakes?orgId=1&var-tenant=brighthealth
- Control plane event: cp-event-2026-03-10-141203 (included in attachments).
- Customer-provided HAR with timing headers attached (har_brighthealth_0310.har).

Additional notes:
- Customer observes correlation with CDN prefetch TTL (60s) and our residency stamp rotation (every 45s during the reconciliation window).
- No model output degradation reported.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:35 - Aisha Khan (Support): Acknowledged, escalated to SRE. Requested full edge/TLS logs and control-plane event timestamps. Notified customer about ongoing investigation and requested a non-prod repro if available.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Marco Silva (SRE): Confirmed spike in TLS full-handshakes for tenant brighthealth between 14:12 and 14:35 UTC. Observed SNI header switching on the same token across consecutive requests. Pulling routing-reconciler timeline.

2026-03-10 15:20 - Elena Park (Networking): Hypothesis: control-plane stamp rotation timing overlapped with CDN prefetch cache TTL causing dual-edge mappings. Proposed to throttle residency-rollover for dedicated tenants to avoid sub-ttl rotations. Filing ops task for change in reconciler cadence.

2026-03-11 09:12 - BrightHealth AI (Customer): Provided HAR traces and observed increased TLS handshake times only when client uses their EU-based origination. Confirmed that toggling strict residency off removes the extra latency in our tests.

2026-03-12 10:01 - Marco Silva (SRE): Test deploy of reconciler delay merged to canary (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2118). Early canary results show handshake counts reduced by ~78% for the tenant during a 1 hour run. Planning staged rollout to dedicated clusters.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Aisha Khan (Support): Communicated workaround to customer (delay rotation + enable session affinity at CDN). Customer accepted temporary mitigation while we complete rollout. Scheduled follow-up in 48 hours.
investigation_notes: Collected edge-proxy and api-gateway metrics: spikes coincide exactly with stamp rotation windows (14:12, 14:55).
Found CDN prefetch TTL of 60s (customer-configured). Our reconciler had 45s rotation cadence during recent control-plane repair, creating a window where two edge mappings were valid for short period.
Observed session-affinity headers differ between hits; when SNI flips, session cache lookup fails -> full TLS handshake. This explains latency delta without 5xxs.
Reproducer built in staging by simulating stamp rotation at 30s intervals with CDN TTL 60s and saw 2.4x TLS handshake rate and p95 handshake time increase.
Canary of reconciler-delay change reduced handshake count and p95 latency for the tenant. No negative impact observed on failover time in canary window.
Related items: need to audit other tenants with short CDN TTL + recent reconciler change to ensure no regression.

Next steps: schedule reconciler cadence config change for dedicated clusters, coordinate with CDN team to expose session-affinity controls to tenant, add alert on handshake-rate anomaly for tenant-scoped windows.
resolution: Workaround applied: delayed residency-stamp rotation cadence for BrightHealth AI dedicated cluster and advised customer to enable CDN session affinity for their origin. Permanent fix: control-plane reconciler cadence change merged (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2118) and scheduled for staged rollout across Dedicated clusters on 2026-03-14. Monitoring: created tenant-scoped TLS-handshake-rate alert (runbook linked in Confluence). Follow-ups: INT ticket to audit other dedicated tenants and add an integration test covering CDN-TTL vs residency-rotation interactions (INT-4502). Customer notified and will confirm stability in 48 hours.
